# Independent canonical-CBOR oracle

`python_oracle.json` is generated by `scripts/kv_cbor_oracle.py` with Python's
`hashlib` and **cbor2 5.6.5**, independently of the Rust CBOR encoder. The
synthetic inputs are newly authored and distributed under this repository's
Apache-2.0 license. They include values outside the model vocabulary solely to
test serialization boundaries; they are not inference requests.

The serialization contract follows vLLM's
[`sha256_cbor`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/utils/hashing.py)
and [`init_none_hash` / `hash_block_tokens`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.29.0/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py)
at v0.29.0, with an explicit `PYTHONHASHSEED`:

1. Hash the canonical-CBOR encoding of the decimal `PYTHONHASHSEED` string.
2. For each complete block, hash canonical CBOR of
   `(parent_hash_bytes, tuple(token_ids), None)`.
3. Feed the resulting 32-byte hash into the next block's parent field.

The fixture tests block size 16; seeds 0 and 42; integer boundaries
23/24, 255/256, 65535/65536 and u32::MAX; Qwen special-token IDs; two chained
blocks; and three ignored trailing token IDs. CBOR bytes are included alongside
the hashes so reviewers can inspect the exact representation. This is an
independent serialization oracle, not a claim of actual vLLM execution or a
passed candidate Rust test.

Reproduce in an isolated Linux environment:

```sh
python -m pip install cbor2==5.6.5
python scripts/kv_cbor_oracle.py --check tests/fixtures/kv_cbor/python_oracle.json
```

Omit `--check` to print the oracle. The Rust unit test
`kv_index::block_hash::tests::sha256_cbor_matches_python_integer_boundaries_and_seeds`
compares the production hash generator with this fixture without invoking
Python, networking, or loading a model.
